subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed channel turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: The source has narrow replay-safe retry and restart-marker pieces, but the remaining behavior crosses Codex transport semantics, replay safety, Gateway lifecycle, and message delivery policy.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define one policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused restart and Codex harness tests.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime fail-closed behavior but make the user-facing message and logs distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue under needs-live-repro until a current-main long-maintenance run proves the remaining transport-close trigger.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define one policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused restart and Codex harness tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current retry boundary and adjacent restart-recovery ownership both trace through their recent merged work, making this the strongest routing owner.
